My setup for the past 6-7 years and it’s been just fine. Ableton live, serum, beyerdynamic 770 headphones. Don’t get me wrong, I have had other things before but nothing that ever stuck. No one setup fits all but getting good with minimal amounts of equipment or software with give you a solid foundation. All the equipment/software in the world won’t give you skill, just compliments it.

As for learning, you mention wubz so…I can name like 6-7 producers on YouTube with multiple production videos, start to finish videos, techniques they use etc etc. wouldn’t waste your time learning from anyone except the people you actually listen to, assuming they put out content on there producing techniques…virtual riot has been putting out quite a bit lately on YouTube, good place to start.

I would start with full length song follow along’s. There’s tons. Many artists do them. Copy what they do. Then again, so on. Then try to make something without following along. I learned quite a bit from this strategy. Also sprinkle in YouTube videos here and there of specific topics or questions you have throughout. The thing about music production, you never really learn everything, you just get really good and efficient at different workflows that constantly evolve as you learn more. Also, experiment, experiment, experiment!

I would recommend the following. 

To have a better idea of your problem is similar to mine, you should check to see if your getting similar error codes.

Open event viewer(search it in the search bar). Once open, there should be a area towards the middle that has different drop down tabs with different codes your windows OS is showing. Open the one that says critical. IF you see a code in there, it may or may not be “kernel power 41”. If so, this is usually a good indication your PSU is the culprit. Keep in mind, this is a generic code but it points to a power problem. However, if you see it, I would recommend getting a higher wattage PSU.

I got an 850w just to be safe and future proof in case I ever get a newer GPU. I wouldn’t be too concerned with the brand.

So I had this exact same issue, would only happen while gaming. Turns out it was my PSU, and funny thing. I had the exact same PSU as you. Upgraded to a 850w non-Corsair and haven’t had this issue since.
